outcome: admission to special care nursery or neonatal intensive care unit (SCN/NICU)
cohort: The study included all vertex singleton, uncomplicated pregnancies from 37 to 41 weeks' gestation in Victoria, Australia, from 2012 to 2019.
finding: Induction of labor was associated with an increased risk of cesarean birth, instrumental birth, and admission to the SCN/NICU in many situations without an improvement in perinatal mortality rates for various maternal region of birth groups.
mod_finding: IOL at 38 weeks was associated with an increasing risk of cesarean birth for Australian, New Zealand, Oceanic, African, and South-East Asian and East Asian-born women, with a higher risk for South Asian-born women at 39 weeks; additionally, the risk of instrumental birth varied by gestational week and maternal region of birth when compared to expectant management.
